extracted.intended_audience: registered patent practitioners (patent agents/attorneys), their counsel, and USPTO enrollment & discipline / examination staff
extracted.subtask_description: Standards and procedural requirements governing practitioner conduct before the USPTO, including signature rules, interview/representation rules, duties (competence, diligence, candor, supervision), investigative/cooperation obligations, and consequences of consenting to exclusion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authority to approve resignation and exclude practitioner
rubrics_metrics.description: Pursuant to 35 U.S.C. §§ 2(b)(2)(D) and 32 and 37 C.F.R. §§ 11.19 and 11.27, the USPTO Director has the authority to approve a Declaration of Resignation and to exclude a practitioner on consent from practice before the Office.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Final Order notes that the Director received a Declaration of Resignation pursuant to 37 C.F.R. § 11.27 and approved it, resulting in exclusion on consent commencing on the date of the Final Order.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amendments and other papers must be signed by practitioner or applicant (37 C.F.R. § 1.33(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: Amendments and other papers, except certain written assertions, filed in an application must be signed by a patent practitioner of record, a patent practitioner not of record who acts in a representative capacity, or the applicant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Unless otherwise specified, all papers submitted on behalf of a juristic entity must be signed by a patent practitioner. The Final Order cites this as a fundamental signature requirement and basis for alleging impermissible signature practice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Signature form requirements (37 C.F.R. § 1.4(d))
rubrics_metrics.description: All correspondence, except as provided in 37 C.F.R. §§ 1.4(d)(2)-(d)(4), must be filed with an original handwritten signature personally signed, or a direct or indirect copy of an original.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Order emphasizes the form-of-signature rules and that noncompliant signature forms on filings (e.g., not personally signed) are contrary to §1.4(d).

rubrics_metrics.name: Electronic signature methods and personal entry (37 C.F.R. § 1.4(d)(2)-(d)(4))
rubrics_metrics.description: Correspondence may, in certain circumstances, be signed electronically under §§ 1.4(d)(2)-(d)(4); when an electronic signature method is used, the signature must be personally entered by the named signatory.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Order notes electronic signatures are permitted only in specified ways and require personal entry by the named signatory—use outside those conditions can be improper.

rubrics_metrics.name: Certification when inserting a signature electronically (37 C.F.R. § 1.4(d)(5)(ii))
rubrics_metrics.description: A person inserting a signature under §§ 1.4(d)(2)-(d)(4) certifies that the inserted signature is his or her own. A person submitting a document signed by another under those paragraphs must have a reasonable basis to believe the signature was actually inserted by that person and should retain evidence of authenticity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practitioners or filers using inserted electronic signatures must retain evidence of authenticity and have a reasonable basis to believe the signature's provenance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Practitioner certification of factual contentions (37 C.F.R. § 11.18(b)(2))
rubrics_metrics.description: A practitioner presenting a document to the USPTO certifies that to the best of the practitioner’s knowledge, formed after an inquiry reasonable under the circumstances, the factual contentions made in the document have evidentiary support.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is cited as a ground for alleging misconduct where filings contained factual assertions without adequate inquiry or evidentiary support.

rubrics_metrics.name: Only registered practitioners may represent others in patent matters (37 C.F.R. §§ 11.6 and 11.10)
rubrics_metrics.description: With few exceptions, only practitioners who are registered under 37 C.F.R. § 11.6 ("patent practitioners") are permitted to represent others before the Office in patent matters; § 11.10 affirms this limitation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Communications and interviews about pending applications should be with an authorized/registered representative; communications with unregistered individuals are generally forbidden.

rubrics_metrics.name: USPTO examiner interviews conducted with patent practitioners (37 C.F.R. § 1.133(a))
rubrics_metrics.description: USPTO examiners may conduct interviews with patent practitioners concerning patent applications and other patent matters pending before the Office.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Order references interviews and the expectation that authorized practitioner representatives attend; non-practitioner attendance is highlighted as impermissible.

rubrics_metrics.name: MPEP guidance on communications with unregistered persons (MPEP § 713.05)
rubrics_metrics.description: Office employees are forbidden to hold either oral or written communication with an unregistered or a suspended or excluded attorney or agent regarding an application unless it is one in which said attorney or agent is the applicant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The MPEP notes that many interview requests come from persons of informal credentials, and examiners must restrict substantive communications to authorized practitioners; cited as supporting the prohibition on unregistered assistants attending interviews.

rubrics_metrics.name: Information Disclosure Statement signature requirement (reference to 37 C.F.R. § 1.33 and § 1.4(d))
rubrics_metrics.description: The signature block for Information Disclosure Statements states that a signature of the applicant or representative is required in accordance with CFR 1.33; see CFR 1.4(d) for the form of the signature.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: IDS forms require practitioner or applicant signatures in compliance with the signature rules; allowing non-practitioners to sign IDSs was alleged as misconduct.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authorization for Internet Communications signature requirement (reference to 37 C.F.R. § 1.33 and § 1.4)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Authorization For Internet Communications signature block states: 'This form must be signed in accordance with 37 CFR 1.33. See 37 CFR 1.4 for signature requirement and certifications.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Order cites instances where non-practitioners signed this form on behalf of the practitioner, contrary to signature rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Issue fee payment form signature requirement (reference to 37 C.F.R. § 1.33 and § 1.4)
rubrics_metrics.description: The signature block for the Issue Fee form states: 'This form must be signed in accordance with 37 CFR 1.33. See 37 CFR 1.4 for signature requirement and certifications.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Filing issue fee forms requires appropriate signatory; non-practitioner signings were cited as impermissible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Terminal disclaimer signature requirement (37 C.F.R. § 1.321(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: A Terminal Disclaimer must be signed by the applicant or an attorney or agent of record (37 C.F.R. § 1.321(b)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Order alleges non-practitioner assistants signed terminal disclaimers improperly; the regulation specifies who may sign.

rubrics_metrics.name: Obligation to establish office policies/procedures preventing impermissible assistant conduct
rubrics_metrics.description: Practitioners must establish and enforce policies and procedures that ensure non-practitioner assistants do not impermissibly sign documents or conduct interviews; failure to do so can violate supervision and competence/diligence rules.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Order repeatedly states Respondent 'did not establish policies and procedures' to prevent impermissible signing/communications and that this failure supports allegations under § 11.503 (supervision), § 11.101 (competence), and § 11.103 (diligence).

rubrics_metrics.name: Supervision obligations (37 C.F.R. § 11.503(a) and (b))
rubrics_metrics.description: A practitioner must adequately supervise non-practitioner assistants with whom the practitioner is associated and make reasonable efforts to ensure they comply with USPTO signature, certification, and interview rules (37 C.F.R. § 11.503(a) and (b)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Failure to supervise assistants who signed filings or attended interviews was charged as misconduct under these provisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Duty of candor to the tribunal (37 C.F.R. §§ 11.303(a)(1), 11.303(a)(3), 11.303(d))
rubrics_metrics.description: Practitioners must be candid to the tribunal; allowing documents to be filed that the practitioner knew were not signed by the named signatory or not in compliance with signature/certification rules violates candor obligations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Complaint alleges Respondent violated the duty of candor by allowing noncompliant-signed documents to be filed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Competence standard (37 C.F.R. § 11.101)
rubrics_metrics.description: Practitioners must provide competent representation to a client; failing to prevent non-practitioner assistants from impermissibly signing or conducting interviews can constitute lack of competence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Order frames allowing non-practitioner signatures and interviews as among the acts constituting failure to provide competent representation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Diligence and promptness (37 C.F.R. § 11.103)
rubrics_metrics.description: Practitioners must act with reasonable diligence and promptness in representing a client; permitting unauthorized assistant actions or failing to put adequate procedures in place can violate this duty.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Complaint alleges lack of diligence where administrative convenience was used to permit assistant signatures rather than timely ensuring authorized signatures by the practitioner.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assisting unauthorized practice (37 C.F.R. § 11.505)
rubrics_metrics.description: Assisting another in the unauthorized practice of law or practice before the USPTO—e.g., by allowing non-practitioner assistants to sign submissions or conduct interviews—is prohibited under § 11.505.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Order alleges Respondent's conduct amounted to assisting unauthorized practice by permitting non-practitioner assistants to perform practitioner-only acts.

rubrics_metrics.name: False statements and failure to cooperate (37 C.F.R. § 11.801(a) and (b))
rubrics_metrics.description: Knowingly making a false statement of material fact (11.801(a)) and failing to cooperate with OED's investigation (11.801(b)) are violations; providing misleading responses or failing to produce requested documents/itineraries are examples.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Complaint alleges Respondent provided false information regarding employment and did not provide requested lists of documents signed by non-practitioners or relevant travel itineraries.

rubrics_metrics.name: Engaging in dishonesty, fraud, deceit, or misrepresentation (37 C.F.R. § 11.804(c))
rubrics_metrics.description: Practitioner conduct involving dishonesty, fraud, deceit, or misrepresentation violates § 11.804(c); allowing filings signed by others or providing false information to OED are cited as examples.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Order lists § 11.804(c) among rules alleged to be violated by the respondent’s actions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conduct prejudicial to administration of justice (37 C.F.R. § 11.804(d))
rubrics_metrics.description: Conduct that is prejudicial to the administration of justice—such as permitting non-practitioners to sign filings or not cooperating with investigations—violates § 11.804(d).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Complaint alleges prejudice to the administration of justice by permitting misrepresentations and noncompliant filings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conduct adversely reflecting on fitness to practice (37 C.F.R. § 11.804(i))
rubrics_metrics.description: Engaging in other conduct that adversely reflects on a practitioner’s fitness to practice before the USPTO is prohibited under § 11.804(i).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Order includes § 11.804(i) to capture other acts or omissions not specifically enumerated but that reflect adversely on fitness to practice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Practitioner must retain evidence of signature authenticity
rubrics_metrics.description: When relying on certain electronic signature insertions, the person submitting the document must retain evidence of the signature's authenticity and have a reasonable basis to believe the signature was actually inserted by the named person (37 C.F.R. § 1.4(d)(5)(ii)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recordkeeping and proof of signature provenance are required when signatures are not original handwritten signatures personally signed by the named signatory.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consequences of consenting to exclusion (37 C.F.R. § 11.27(a)(3))
rubrics_metrics.description: A practitioner who consents to exclusion under § 11.27 acknowledges that if and when he applies for reinstatement under § 11.60, the OED Director will conclusively presume for purposes of reinstatement that the facts alleged in the complaint are true and that the practitioner could not have successfully defended against the charges.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Respondent's Declaration of Resignation acknowledged this presumption and the legal consequences of consenting to exclusion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication and notice requirements following exclusion
rubrics_metrics.description: The OED Director shall electronically publish the Final Order in the OED electronic FOIA Reading Room and publish a notice in the Official Gazette materially consistent with the provided notice text.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Final Order specifies publication venues and includes a model notice describing the allegations, rules allegedly violated, and the practitioner's consent/exclusion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Obligation to comply with reinstatement procedural rules (37 C.F.R. §§ 11.58 and 11.60)
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent shall comply fully with 37 C.F.R. § 11.58 and shall comply fully with 37 C.F.R. § 11.60 upon any request for reinstatement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Order imposes compliance obligations tied to future reinstatement proceedings and other applicable reinstatement/regulatory provisions.
